title: Antipode of a Hopf Algebra Is Anti-Multiplicative
body_html:
Antipode of a Hopf Algebra Is Anti-Multiplicative

Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(A\) an \(R\)-Hopf algebra with antipode \(S : A \to A\). For all \(a, b \in A\),

\[ S(a \cdot b) \;=\; S(b) \cdot S(a). \]
proof_html:
The standard argument uses uniqueness of inverses in the convolution algebra. Consider the convolution algebra \(\operatorname{End}_R(A \otimes_R A, A)\) with convolution multiplication coming from the coalgebra structure on \(A \otimes A\) and the algebra structure on \(A\). The multiplication map \(\mu : A \otimes A \to A\) is an element of this algebra. We exhibit two convolution-inverses of \(\mu\) and conclude they are equal:

  1. \(\mu \circ (S \otimes S) \circ \tau\), where \(\tau\) is the tensor-swap, satisfies \(\mu * (\mu \circ (S \otimes S) \circ \tau) = \eta \circ \varepsilon \circ \mu\), by direct Sweedler computation using the antipode axiom on each factor.
  2. \(S \circ \mu\) satisfies the analogous identity by a similar computation, using that \(\varepsilon\) is multiplicative (\(\varepsilon(ab) = \varepsilon(a) \varepsilon(b)\), the bialgebra axiom).

Convolution inverses in an algebra are unique, hence the two maps are equal: \(S \circ \mu = \mu \circ (S \otimes S) \circ \tau\), i.e.\ \(S(ab) = S(b) S(a)\).
\(\square\)

Mathlib state. This lemma is now proved directly at the ring-theoretic level as \(\texttt{HopfAlgebra.antipode\_mul}\) in \(\texttt{Mathlib.RingTheory.HopfAlgebra.Basic}\). The project exposes the same theorem under \(\texttt{Langlands.AlgebraicGeometry.HopfAntipode.antipode\_anti\_multiplicativity}\) so downstream nodes do not depend on Mathlib naming details.

Project use. For affine group schemes we usually use the commutative-source specialization, [[node:affine_group_schemes.antipode_multiplicativity_commutative_hopf|the multiplicativity statement \(S(ab) = S(a) S(b)\)]], which follows from anti-multiplicativity plus commutativity of the coordinate ring.
